item.title: Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Playoff stakes are high in this emerging SEC rivalry
item.description: The College Football Playoff has altered the trajectory of the sport in so many ways, and the 24-team bracket will cause even more chaos . But one immediate benefit is that the CFP creates instant blood rivalries; there’s nothing quite like the prospect of ending another team’s season to fire up the blood. Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) and Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC), which meet this weekend in a crucial SEC game, last lined up against one another on the first day of 2026 in the Sugar Bowl, and what resulted was an absolutely spectacular, 14-score game that was in doubt until literally the final seconds of the game. Ole Miss won, 39-34, but only after Georgia had tied the game with 56 seconds remaining. The stakes when these two teams meet on Saturday in Oxford aren’t quite so existential, but close. Georgia, ranked No. 2 in the initial CFP rankings, should be fine to make the playoff even with a loss, but Ole Miss, at No. 10, could be in trouble. Whoever wins gets an easier path to the SEC championship and its coveted first-round bye. At this point in the season, everyone knows what’s what, and it’s just a matter of executing. And for both teams, it’s a matter of containment — for Ole Miss, containing Georgia’s run game; for Georgia, containing Ole Miss’ do-everything quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. Trinidad Chambliss will be the key to Ole Miss' chances of upsetting Georgia on Saturday. Justin Ford via Getty Images Kirby Smart, in the midst of his usual glossing of the next week’s opponent, lasered in on what makes Chambliss so difficult to defend against. “It's not the ‘wow!’ plays. The wow plays are what you guys love and what America loves,” he told assembled media earlier this week. “It's the down-in, down-out decision making that he's really elite at. The accuracy that he's elite at, the release, the decision. His pinpointing. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched. … He goes forwards, backwards as fast as he goes sideways.” Chambliss, to Smart’s mind, presents a unique challenge because of his talent, his experience, and his system under head coach Pete Golding. “There's nothing we're going to do that he hasn't seen,” Smart said. “You're not tricking the guy. I think that's what people get infatuated with, is, ‘How can I trick him and do that?’ You can't do that. … There's not a perfect remedy. If there was, somebody would have done it.” The Rebels are averaging 282.1 yards through the air this season, second only to LSU in the SEC. Georgia’s defense ranks sixth in the conference, giving up 186.6 yards through the air per game. But pure yardage doesn’t tell the full story; Chambliss is lethal in the red zone, making plays that give even Smart pause — “not against the Sisters of the Poor, he’s doing that against SEC teams. That makes him hard to defend in the red area.” On the plus side for the Georgia defense, the Bulldogs are swarming quarterbacks at a fearsome rate — 26 sacks to date, the program’s best since the landmark defe

item.title: Browns injuries: Deshaun Watson update as 2 of 4 starters return to practice
item.description: As the Cleveland Browns prepare for the New Orleans Saints, the official injury reports each day look like they will provide a lot of information about how Week 9 will go. On Wednesday, the Browns announced that QB Deshaun Watson was in concussion protocol , with QB Shedeur Sanders likely to start in his place . Along with Watson, four Cleveland starters missed the first practice of the wee k. On the other side, the Saints saw WR Jordyn Tyson and OT Kelvin Banks Jr. return to practice with a chance to return from injured reserve this week. On Thursday, Watson was not at practice, and DT Maliek Collins was still sidelined, but OT Austin Barber and LB Quincy Williams returned to the practice field in Berea. Some good news for Cleveland’s chances in Week 9, but Collins is a big part of the team’s defensive line. As we saw last week with OT Tytus Howard , it is possible for a veteran to miss practices and still play against the Saints, but Friday’s participation report could be a huge indicator of Collins’ ability to play. We will have the full injury report later this afternoon. Is Barber or Collins a bigger return for the Browns? Join the conversation! item.title: Max Verstappen jokes about rain threat in Brazil: "I've installed antivirus now!"
item.description: Motorsport photo The first wet race with Formula 1’s 2026 cars did not exactly prove to be a resounding success. During the formation laps behind the safety car at the Sepang International Circuit, almost half the field came to a halt. The issue turned out to be a software bug linked to the 250kW restrictions imposed by the FIA for wet-weather races. That software bug caused the electric motors to go into lock-down mode in the slowest parts of the circuit. With no electric power available to offset the turbo lag, nothing happened when the drivers pressed the throttle pedal. In Malaysia, the restrictions were lifted for the most problematic minisectors, with the FIA sending new software to the teams and manufacturers after approximately 20 minutes. They were then able to install the updated version in their power units to finally get the race under way. The same emergency measure was subsequently applied in Singapore, before a test with modified software followed in Austin. At the Circuit of the Americas, the FIA issued the following statement: "As part of the ongoing refinements to the Power Unit software for low grip mode, the FIA together with the teams and Power Unit manufacturers will run a simulation at the end of FP1, with cars running on low grip mode, using specific driver inputs during the in-lap to test additional software protections. This will mean that cars will be running for a short distance at low speed at Turn 15 at the end of the session." FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis had already explained in Malaysia that the bug had only come to light during the race because the FIA had not been able to carry out sufficient testing with the 2026 cars in wet conditions beforehand. In response to a question from Motorsport.com, he confirmed that he could guarantee this specific bug would not occur again, although he added that he could not rule out all bugs. Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team, Alexander Albon, Williams, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team, Alexander Albon, Williams, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Given the weather forecast for Sao Paulo, there is a possibility that F1 drivers will once again encounter rain this weekend. Asked during the FIA press conference whether the drivers are confident that the Sepang debacle will not be repeated, Max Verstappen joked: "I have installed antivirus in my car, so I'll be fine!" When Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad then said that he hoped the issue had been resolved, Verstappen picked up the microphone once more and laughed: "You'll be on the same software, mate, so don't worry!" Verstappen has fond memories of Interlagos in both dry and wet conditions. The Red Bull driver has won there three times and has produced memorable comeback drives on just as many occasions. item.title: WTA apologizes as recording aired of Pegula calling Andreeva a 'diva'
item.description: FILE PHOTO - US tennis player Jessica Pegula celebrates defeating Polish Iga Świątek during their women's singles final match of the Bad Homburg Open Tennis Tournament. (is associated with: «WTA apologizes as recording aired of Pegula calling Andreeva a 'diva'») Arne Dedert/dpa The WTA women's tennis tour has apologized and admitted it did not tell players their on-court conversations during practice sessions at the WTA Finals were being broadcast. A furore has broken out in Indian Wells after Jessica Pegula was heard on the WTA’s YouTube livestream making derogatory comments about Mirra Andreeva and her coach Conchita Martinez. A spokesperson for the governing body said on Thursday: “The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players’ practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals. “We sincerely apologize for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed.” The tour had intended for the microphones to capture ambient sounds from the court and has acknowledged it failed to ensure the appropriate safeguards were in place. A conversation between Pegula and her coach Mark Knowles has been widely scrutinized, with the US world number five critiquing the attitude of third-ranked Russian teenager Andreeva. Pegula can clearly be heard calling the 19-year-old a “diva” and saying she has lost respect for former Wimbledon champion Martinez for not calling out her behaviour. Pegula goes on to say Andreeva would be better than her fellow American Coco Gauff if she had the same mentality. Another practice session, meanwhile, saw world number one Elena Rybakina having an apparent spat with her coach. The WTA said it would continue to livestream practice sessions but without any audio. The WTA Finals, which features the best eight singles players and doubles teams of the year, begins on Sunday. Pegula and Andreeva have been drawn in different groups and cannot meet until the semi-finals. The incidents follow a debate at the Australian Open in January around the broadcasting of backstage areas, with Gauff annoyed after being filmed smashing her racket in what she thought was a private area. Gauff called for more privacy, while former world number one Iga Świątek said players were being treated like animals in a zoo.

item.title: Muse has a voice mode now
item.description: Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today . The feature has been rolled out to me, and I gave it a spin on the iOS app while writing this article. As you chat with your Muse agent, the avatar at the top of your conversation animates in time with the words that it's saying. You can also change the tone of the voice by just asking your agent about what you want and letting it decide or by browsing through a bunch of options in the avatar settings. item.title: How Jonathan Gannon built a Top-5 Packers defense without Micah Parsons
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co If you’re reading this, you obviously know that on Aug. 28, 2025, the Green Bay Packers traded defensive tackle Kenny Clark, and first-round picks in 2026 and 2027, to the Dallas Cowboys for the services of transcendent edge-rusher Micah Parsons. And when the 2025 season began, it appeared to foster a major improvement in Jeff Hafley’s defense. In the first half of the 2025 season, Green Bay’s defense ranked 10th in DVOA and Parsons was on a tear. Through Week 15 of the 2025 season, he totaled 14 sacks and 79 pressures, looking every bit the force he had been with Dallas. Then, in Week 15 against the Denver Broncos, Parsons suffered a torn ACL, and things quickly fell apart for the Pack on Parsons’ side of the ball — and overall. The previously 9-3-1 Pack lost every game from then on, and their season ended abruptly with a 31-27 Wild Card playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. There wasn’t enough juice without their defensive epicenter to get things done. The Packers fell to 25th in Defensive DVOA in the second half of the season, and a primary reason was pretty clear. With Parsons on the field (669 snaps): 4.87 yards allowed per play EPA/play allowed: -0.048 (favorable for the defense) Pass defense: 367 attempts, 6.29 yards per attempt allowed Run defense: 273 attempts, 4.13 yards per carry allowed 29 sacks, 6 interceptions Without Parsons on the field (469 snaps): 5.31 yards allowed per play EPA/play allowed: +0.09 (unfavorable for the defense) Pass defense: 230 attempts, 6.82 yards per attempt allowed Run defense: 231 attempts, 4.18 yards per carry allowed 8 sacks, 3 interceptions “We just need to get healthy,” Parsons told me on September 16 , three days after the Packers lost their season opener to the Minnesota Vikings, 39-22. “I think once we get healthy, and I’m back on that grass or that turf, we’re going to take it to another level.” Thing is, new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon couldn’t wait around for Parsons to get healthy. The hope was that he’d be ready by Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Cowboys, but that didn’t happen. Gannon had to do the best he could with what he had. And the extent to which he’s done that is one of the NFL’s most impressive stories in the 2026 season. The Packers currently rank fourth in Defensive DVOA , and Gannon’s concepts have been profoundly unsettling to their opponents. So, how is Gannon doing so well in a new environment, with players he didn’t know last season? Everything is working at all three levels. Creative pressures help everybody get to the quarterback As you would expect, Gannon is blitzing at a pretty high rate (31.9% this season, 12th-highest in the NFL) to maximize pressure, but Green Bay’s pressure rate of 38.7% is only 18th-highest, per SumerSports. Lukas Van Ness leads the team with five sacks and 28 total pressures. Rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton is second with four sacks, and fellow edge-rusher Brenton Cox Jr. is second with 22 pressures. item.title: Donegal great Murphy retires from inter-county football
item.description: Murphy scored 1-4 in the 2012 All-Ireland final as Donegal beat Mayo to win the Sam Maguire [Getty Images] Donegal's All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy has announced his retirement from inter-county football for the second time. The 37-year-old made his Donegal debut in 2007 and captained the county to All-Ireland success in 2012, scoring 1-4 as they beat Mayo in the decider. The Glenswilly forward also won six Ulster Senior Football titles, including back-to-back triumphs in 2018 and 2019, and is a four-time All Star. He previously announced his inter-county retirement in 2022, but reversed the decision two years later and made a triumphant return under Jim McGuinness in the 2025 season. He helped his county to retain the Anglo-Celt Cup with an extra-time victory against Armagh and reach the All-Ireland final, which they lost to Kerry. His stellar performances earned him a fourth All-Star while he was also nominated for the Footballer of the Year award that year. Murphy stayed on for the 2026 season and while Donegal won the Division One title, his last game was their All-Ireland round-three exit to Dublin in June. "The Donegal County Board has today announced that former All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy has retired from inter-county football," the county said in a statement. "The player informed management in recent weeks once the club championship had concluded. "Michael has been Donegal's talisman for a generation and captained the county for most of his career having made his senior debut back in 2007. Two seasons ago, he came out of retirement, winning a sixth Ulster medal, his fourth All-Star and a national league title in the process." 'One of the giants of the modern game' Paying tribute to Murphy's decorated inter-county career, Donegal county board chairperson Mary Coughlan added: "Alas, we always knew this day would come but we are privileged to have watched the stellar career of Michael Murphy up close. "What he has given Donegal GAA on-and-off the field is simply extraordinary while always an ambassador par excellence and role-model for so many young people in our county and beyond. "He is one of the giants of the modern game and when players talk about leaving the jersey in a better place on retiring, Michael has certainly done that. He has carried himself with tremendous dignity and integrity at all times. "His innate modesty is a foil for a fierce competitor who never gave less than 100% while inspiring others around him to do likewise." Murphy's retirement is a further blow for boss McGuinness, who decided to remain at the helm for a fourth year in his second stint. He has also lost talented defender Finnbarr Roarty after the 2025 Young Footballer of the Year signed a two-year rookie contract with Aussie Rules outfit Collingwood.

item.title: Men’s Soccer: Northwestern stuns No. 13 Wisconsin in season closer
item.description: In their final matchup of the year the Wildcats (6-6-4, 3-4-3 B1G) closed out their season with a 3-1 win at home against No. 13 Wisconsin (10-3-4, 3-3-4 B1G), their second victory against a top-15 opponent this season. Entering the game, Northwestern was already out of the Big Ten Tournament due to its loss to Ohio State on Nov. 1, but Wisconsin still had hope, needing a win against the ‘Cats and some help from other teams to secure it a spot. However, the Wildcats quickly proved they weren’t going to give up a win easily, no matter how badly the Badgers wanted it. With a hat trick by senior Peter Riesz in his final game as a Wildcat, and six saves by goalie Dominic Pereira, the ‘Cats were able to come from behind and stun the Badgers and their tournament hopes, taking down Wisconsin for the first time since October 2021. Opening up the game, the Badgers were ready to start fast, as they recorded the first shot in the fourth minute, off the foot of Wilmette local Markie Hrvojevic, though the attempt missed the mark. From there, it remained quiet on shots until the 14th minute, when Wisconsin’s Emile Kisse shot wide of the goal after a diving tip by Pereira. From there it was back and forth between the teams, including a blast from NU’s Bryant Mayer that was saved. The continued stalemate between the two teams came to an end in the 33rd minute when Wisconsin got the first goal after an Aiden Martinez cross resulted in a Roman Eisa header, which found the back of the net, putting the No. 13 team up in the first half. Minutes later it seemed that the ‘Cats were able to tie the game up, only for the game-tying goal by Aaron O’Reilly to be called back due to a foul in the buildup. In the minutes before half, the ‘Cats had another opportunity to equalize when a corner from Tre Barrett almost found the net, but barely went over the goal. Going into the half, the red and white were up 1-0, having outshot the Wildcats 5-3. At the start of the second half, the Badgers maintained their momentum on goal. Wisco threatened the net, but the ’Cats kept them out of goal, with Pereira coming up with a huge point-blank save of Martinez. With the Badgers in striking distance, the Wildcats needed to strike and in the 58th minute they finally did that with a penalty kick following a Wisconsin foul inside the 18-yard box. It was Riesz who was able to crush the ball into the net and tie things up for the purple and white. As soon as the Wildcats scored, there was continued pressure from there, with three ‘Cats forcing saves out of Wisconsin just minutes later. Eventually, the continued pressure came to fruition, as the ‘Cats cashed in again in the 70th minute when Riesz smashed a right-footed attempt from 15 yards out with assists from Ethan Nakolo and Seth Mahlmeister. The Wildcats were now on top, 2-1, but continued to play like they were behind with the amount of pressure they continued to put on the Badgers. item.title: Nick Bosa says ‘I feel great’ and ‘I’m ready to go’
item.description: (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) San Francisco 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa told reporters , “I feel great” and “I’m ready to go” on Wednesday. Bosa said it’s been tough, but he’s thinking more about the long haul. Bosa spoke about his injury: “It was my other leg. I must’ve had some type of compensation going on, especially in that first week back, just kind of trying to push it back with the tendonitis. So, I may have been favoring it a little bit. I was just doing my normal warm-up drills one day, and I tweaked it. Calves are a pretty long process. I’ve never had one, so it took a little longer than I expected. But I don’t even think about it anymore.” Bosa said the calf injury was unrelated to his Achilles. Bosa also mentioned how he could’ve returned earlier. General manager John Lynch was asked about the long-term strategy and plan for Bosa: We don’t take any game for granted, believe me. We only play 17 of these in the regular season, so they all count immensely. I think what we try to do in every situation is, we get our medical people, the doctors, the trainers, and the player involved. And we kinda look at these injuries from every angle involved, and we push ‘em to try to get them back. And when they’re ready, and there are a bunch of objective numbers to hit, to be able to do that. Nick saying that, he probably felt like he could, but I think all working together, we came to the decision that it was best to wait through Atlanta, to get the bye week and then come back. We’re happy we have him back. He’s obviously a difference maker when he’s out there. It will be great to have Nick out there on the field and making a difference like he always does. For as much talk as there is surrounding DeForest Buckner helping out the defensive tackles, Bosa takes immense pressure off Keion White and Romello Height to be every-down players and playing in situations you otherwise wouldn’t. The line will be fresh, but it will also have top-to-bottom talent we haven’t seen since 2022.

item.title: Miami’s High-Priced QB Loses Top Target Before Notre Dame Clash
item.description: In some ways, it’s hard for Miami’s Malachi Toney to describe how close he’s grown to Darian Mensah in a matter of months. The quarterback-wide receiver combination is one of the most potent 1-2 punches in college football this season and is the main reason why the Hurricanes are the No. 1 team in the initial College Football Playoff rankings released on Tuesday. “It’s just been crazy,” Toney told reporters this week. “We were just in the locker room just talking about how I saw him at [Prime 112 Restaurant] right after he committed. Just him getting adapted to Miami, we’ve grown so close.” That connection was disrupted Wednesday, when Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice and underwent surgery. He’s expected back later this season, but will miss Saturday’s much-anticipated matchup with Notre Dame, No. 11 in the Playoff rankings. But confidence remains high in Coral Gables because Miami has Mensah, who’s proven himself as a leader and competitor within Miami’s program since he arrived. “He’s eager to get the ball,” Miami head coach Mario Cristobal said this week. “Enthusiasm, excited, doesn’t flinch, very focused. Just ready, prepared. It was a preparation to give him that kind of confidence. He’s ready to roll.” Mensah has emerged as one of college football’s biggest stars this season. He’s at his third school in three years, having led Duke to a win in the ACC championship game in 2025 and Tulane to a 9-4 record in 2024. This year he’s been one of the most impactful transfer portal additions in the sport–Mensah leads the nation in touchdown passes (25), and his 80.7% completion percentage would break the NCAA single-season record by more than three points (Bo Nix, 77.4%, 2023). Overall, Miami’s offense leads the nation in scoring at 46.7 points per game. Mensah’s ascension encapsulates how player mobility has changed the sport. Each transfer has led to a bigger on-field opportunity and higher compensation. Mensah arrived at Tulane as a consensus three-star recruit in 2023. He signed a two-year, $8 million deal with Duke in 2024 , one of the biggest in college football at that time. Today, his $6.5 million NIL valuation at Miami is the highest in men’s collegiate athletics, according to On3 . Mensah’s endorsement deals include CVS, Derby Watch Supply, Dr. Pepper, and SlingTV. Saturday’s game at Notre Dame was the predetermined biggest game for Mensah and Miami this season, and Toney’s injury has scaled the challenge by a significant margin. Toney, like Mensah, is a nationwide leader in receiving; he ranks first in catches (73), receiving touchdowns (13), and is second in receiving yards (1,027). Saturday’s game is a huge opportunity for Mensah to showcase his ability without his top weapon. It’s a game that’s been circled for NFL scouts, who’ve been waiting for Mensah to perform against an elite team, and in a primetime slot. item.title: Rumor Makes NY Giants Trading For Derrick Henry Instead of Jonathan Taylor More Realistic Before Deadline
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the New York Giants are reportedly among the teams pursuing a Jonathan Taylor trade, a new rumor adds more steam to the idea that Derrick Henry is the more realistic trade addition before next week’s NFL trade deadline. The Giants are a team to watch over the next week. Heading into the Week 9 NFL schedule, they own a 4-2-1 record and sit atop the NFC East standings. A year ago, they were 2-5 and mentioned as potential sellers before the deadline. Now they have reasons to shop for upgrades to make a serious run at the division title in the second half. The rumblings around the team claim that, along with improving the interior of their defensive line, upgrading the backfield is a goal for the front office before Nov. 10. And according to reports over the weekend, the Giants are competing with the Minnesota Vikings , Green Bay Packers , Cincinnati Bengals , and Denver Broncos in the ongoing Taylor sweepstakes. Although ESPN’s Dan Graziano boldly claimed this week, “I would guess [Taylor] gets traded, and I wouldn’t be at all surprised if it was the Giants who made that move ” the reported asking price is a second-round pick and more, and that could rise if teams are desperate to add the three-time Pro Bowler. That is why the Giants must have alternative options on their wish list. Well, a new report from Jason La Canfora makes a move for the Baltimore Ravens RB make even more sense than his Indianapolis Colts counterpart. Derrick Henry trade may only cost New York Giants a third-round pick Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry (22) runs during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images According to the NFL insider, while some around the league believe Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta would be very hesitant to trade the five-time Pro Bowler, various executives “believe it is the only cogent path to start digging out of a massive roster, payroll, and salary cap hole and begin playing the youngsters on the roster.” Furthermore, one general manager told La Canfora that DeCosta “ could definitely get something for Henry, absolutely .” What would that something be exactly? With Henry having one more season left on his contract , “multiple executives” told the NFL insider that “the Ravens could get third-round value for Henry.” The Giants don’t have a fifth-round pick in 2027 , and their fourth-rounder is a compensatory. However, they do have a third-rounder. They could offer a third-rounder and a future Day 3 pick for Henry. Or try to blow the competition away and offer their second-round pick in 2027. DeCosta has to be willing to trade Henry first. However, Giants head coach John Harbaugh saw the value in the 32-year-old two years ago and pushed Baltimore to trade for him. He could see that same value now and get his old team on the phone and try to persuade them to make a deal over the next week.

item.title: England check on Palmer - what are Tuchel's other big choices?
item.description: Thomas Tuchel will name his next England squad on Friday [Getty Images] England have made medical checks on Cole Palmer as Thomas Tuchel considers whether to select the Chelsea forward in his next squad. The 24-year-old missed all four games during the previous international window with a minor injury. He completed 90 minutes for Chelsea against Brentford before those matches, and started for the Blues in the first game afterwards. Tuchel, who names his squad to face Croatia and Spain on Friday, said at the time that Palmer was "playing with discomfort and pain" but was "missing too many opportunities" with England. Whether he is recalled will be a key theme on Friday. While it is normal for England medics to check on players under consideration, it also underlines that Palmer remains on Tuchel's radar despite his stark comments last month. In addition to deciding whether to select Palmer, head coach Tuchel has a number of other dilemmas to resolve. Bukayo Saka's injury absence opens the door to another attacker, with his Arsenal team-mate Noni Madueke pushing for a recall following a string of impressive performances. Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has not played since mid-October and is not fit for selection, while Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah is a major injury doubt. Defenders Ben White and Djed Spence are pushing for recalls after missing out on the previous squad through injury. The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice and many others are now stonewall selections - but the intrigue is around the remaining few spots still seemingly up for grabs. Will some old faces earn a recall or will there be new faces soon pulling on the England shirt? BBC Sport runs down some of the potential candidates for selection. Josh King The 19-year-old Fulham midfielder has already been close to a senior-team debut. King travelled to the US as part of the preparation squad before the World Cup, along with Alex Scott, Ethan Nwaneri and Rio Ngumoha. Scott and Ngumoha have already made their debuts for the senior side and Nwaneri is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund. Tuchel said in his last press conference how King is close to a senior call-up and the midfielder has impressed for the under-21s too. The biggest challenge for King will be finding a chance to shine in his favoured number 10 position with Bellingham being England's best player and the position being one of real strength for the Three Lions. Will Lankshear Will Lankshear has been prolific for Middlesbrough this season [Press Association] There are a lack of number nines in the English game and the job of being Harry Kane's understudy is harder than it sounds. The England captain has just won the Ballon d'Or, likes to play almost every minute for his country and is the captain, record goalscorer and arguably the best player in Tuchel's side. item.title: NFL viewership stabilizes after early-season declines as league nears midway point
item.description: Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images After some viewership declines during the early portion of the season, the NFL is back on track. Entering Week 9, NFL viewership is up 3% year-over-year, according to a report by Austin Karp in Sports Business Journal . That increase is within the range that could be entirely attributed to Nielsen’s recent methodological changes that altered how the company measured co-viewing , the act of multiple people viewing one telecast in the same room. A recent report by The Athletic’s Stewart Mandel suggested Nielsen’s recent changes raised baseline college football viewership by 3.4% . It’s unclear if the NFL is seeing a similar lift, however. It’s important to note that the league came out publicly against Nielsen’s changes before the seas0n began. NFL telecasts are averaging 18.4 million viewers through Week 8. The two top audiences of the year both belong to the Kansas City Chiefs and CBS. Chiefs-Raiders averaged 28.45 million viewers on the network in October, and last weekend’s Chiefs-Broncos game averaged 28.18 million viewers. Fox holds the next two most-watched contests; Commanders-Cowboys in September (27.21 million viewers) and 49ers-Seahawks in October (26.70 million viewers). Per Karp, CBS is up 5% overall through Week 8, averaging 19.6 million viewers. Thursday Night Football on Prime Video also continues to trend up, averaging 17.6 million viewers per game. Each of its seven telecasts have seen year-over-year gains. ESPN’s Monday Night Football is up 22% versus last year, though it’s unclear if that number is buoyed by last year’s doubleheaders, which depressed ESPN’s per-game average and would make for a more favorable comparison. Figures for Fox’s and NBC’s viewership through Week 8 were not published. In data released to reporters on Thursday, the NFL pointed towards the number of close games as helping viewership this season. 71 games have been decided by one-score margins so far this season, tied with 2022 for the most in NFL history through eight weeks. 38 games have had a game-winning score in the final five minutes or overtime, tied with 2021 for the most through eight weeks. The NFL sent along some interesting stats this AM: •71 games have been decided by one score (8 or fewer points) – tied with 2022 for the most through Week 8 in NFL history. •38 games have featured a game-winning score in the final five minutes of the 4th quarter or OT – tied with 2021 for the most through Week 8 in NFL history. Closer games means higher viewership numbers. — Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 5, 2026 Be it close games, Nielsen changes, or just normal viewership fluctuations, the league likes when ratings go up. And so far this season, the NFL continues to display its strength in viewership. The post NFL viewership stabilizes after early-season declines as league nears midway point appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Arsenal star told why he should consider Bundesliga move
item.description: Arsenal star told why he should consider Bundesliga move Martin Odegaard has been linked with a potential move to Bayern Munich , with the Arsenal captain being advised to consider joining the German giants if an opportunity arises. The Norwegian has established himself as one of the most important players in Mikel Arteta’s squad. He wears the captain’s armband at Arsenal and also leads his country’s national team, underlining his importance at both club and international level. Arsenal have no intention of selling Odegaard or any of their key players, meaning Bayern would face a difficult task if they wanted to bring him to the Bundesliga. The midfielder also appears happy in North London, having produced several impressive performances since becoming an important part of the team. However, reports suggest he could be open to considering a move to Bayern , one of Europe’s leading clubs. Eivind Bisgaard Sundet believes the switch would make sense for the Arsenal captain and has explained why he could benefit from the change. Bayern Munich viewed as a good fit Odegaard’s technical ability and creativity could make him an attractive option for Bayern, particularly given the style of football the German side plays. His ability to influence possession and create opportunities would potentially suit a team that often dominates its domestic matches. There is also the possibility that a move to Germany could offer the midfielder a different physical and competitive schedule compared with the Premier League. Sundet believes those factors could make Bayern an appealing destination if Odegaard ever decides to leave Arsenal. Martin Odegaard v Brentford. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Sundet explains why Odegaard should consider Bayern Speaking about the possibility of the Norwegian joining Bayern, Sundet outlined the benefits he believes the midfielder could enjoy, as quoted by Sports Witness : “I think Bayern would have been a very good fit. “He’d be heavily involved. Playing in German football is a bit less gruelling than in English football. There are slightly fewer matches, you get more time to recover, and Bayern are a more dominant side than Arsenal are in England. You’d have more possession.” Sundet clearly sees Bayern as a club where Odegaard could remain influential while benefiting from a different style of football and schedule. Nevertheless, Arsenal will be keen to retain their captain, and any potential move would depend on whether the midfielder genuinely wants a new challenge. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Henry Cejudo, Kamaru Usman roast Colby Covington for embarrassing 43-second loss: ‘He’s supposed to beat Khamzat Chimaev?‘
item.description: Colby Covington | Chris Unger, Zuffa LLC Colby Covington lasted less than a minute against Raul Rosas Jr. and his peers are letting him have it. Rosas defeated Covington in a submission-only grappling match at a Hype Fighting event in Italy this past Tuesday, needing just 43 seconds to secure a rear-naked choke and force Covington to tap out. It was a stunning upset given Covington’s size advantage (Rosas typically competes at 135 pounds, Covington at 170) and experience as a former interim UFC champion. Longtime Covington rival Kamaru Usman broke down the loss alongside Pound 4 Pound co-host Henry Cejudo, who didn’t hold back with his criticism of Covington. “He gets f*cking taken down, double-legged, this is the whole fight, 40 seconds,” Cejudo said. “Look at this motherf*cker, and he’s supposed to beat Khamzat Chimaev next f*cking week?” Covington wrestles Khamzat Chimaev in the main event of RAF Abu Dhabi next Saturday. Given how Covington fared against a bantamweight, Cejudo is understandably skeptical of his chances against a former UFC middleweight champion. For Usman, who holds two title fight wins over Covington, he was surprised to see the wrestling-minded “Chaos” handled so easily. “First and foremost, I would say this: That’s not excusable because of your name and the brand that you’ve built,” Usman said. “It’s not excusable. Now us, real fighters and competitors, we know how difficult and how different they are. Super different. “Wrestling and jiu-jitsu are completely different. So Raul Rosas caught him off guard, got in there, and put him away.” Fortunately for Covington, the Hype Fighting event might have flew under the radar for the vast majority of fans, so he might receive less backlash than expected for such a disappointing performance. Still, Cejudo and Usman agree that the self-proclaimed “King of Miami” has to show up in his next RAF fight or the damage to his reputation could be far worse. “Colby Covington, you ain’t the king of shit no more,” Cejudo said, later adding, “This does hurt. I guess people will get over it. If he’s able to come out and beat Khamzat Chimaev, people will forget it, or maybe he’ll get a rematch with Raul Rosas, but I think Raul will probably do that shit again to him.” “You could see his face,” Usman said. “He was not ready for that level of intensity right away. For a guy that’s supposed to be intense, he was not ready for that level of intensity.”

item.title: After minor league honors and a lone MLB appearance, Eiberson Castellano is off to free agency
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JUNE 14: Eiberson Castellano #55 of the Colorado Rockies looks on from the pitchers mound in a game against the Athletics during his major league debut at Las Vegas Ballpark on June 14, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Kyle Cooper/Colorado Rockies/Getty Images) Welcome to the 2026 edition of Ranking the Rockies , where we take a look back at every player to log playing time for the Rockies in 2026. The purpose of this list is to provide a snapshot of the player in context. The “Ranking” is an organizing principle that’s drawn from Baseball Reference’s WAR (rWAR). It’s not something the staff debated. We’ll begin with the player with the lowest rWAR and end up with the player with the highest. No. 27, Eiberson Castellano (0.1 rWAR) Eiberson Castellano had a memorable 2026 within the Colorado Rockies system. His 2027, however, will come with another team. The Venezuelan right-handed pitcher signed with the Philadelphia Phillies in 2018 as an international free agent. After skipping the 2019 season and with no minor league season in 2020, he began playing in the Venezuelan Winter League and Dominican Summer League in 2021 before getting some Single-A playing time within the Phillies organization in 2022. He mainly worked within the Philadelphia system for the next few years (with the exception of an offseason stint with the Minnesota Twins after being selected in the Rule 5 draft). He eventually made his way to the Rockies in December 2025. Castellano’s Rockies career lasted just the 2026 season, but he rapidly progressed through the system. In his time in Double-A, he went 4-2 through 10 starts with a 2.72 ERA. Castellano had a stellar June. Early in the month, he was promoted from the Double-A Hartford Yard Goats to the Albuquerque Isotopes, where he pitched six scoreless innings, allowing one hit with seven strikeouts in his Triple-A debut. For that, he was named the Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Week. President of baseball operations Paul DePodesta spoke highly of him following that stretch: “(He) made his first start last night in Triple-A. He had done really, really well in Double-A, had a terrific start last night, went six shutout in his first Triple-A game.” The good times kept rolling. About a week later, the Rockies selected his contract , paving the way for his major league debut. He took the mound in the seventh inning of the wild 23-9 win over the Athletics , hosted at Las Vegas Ballpark. He closed out the game with three innings of work, allowing four hits and no runs with two strikeouts. He was optioned back to Albuquerque the next day. View Link Although the sample size is limited to just 35 pitches in his lone MLB outing, Castellano brought an arsenal of a curveball with good movement, a four-seamer averaging over 95 MPH, and a sinker, with a couple changeups mixed in. item.title: David Ferrer suggested to become Carlos Alcaraz’s new coach soon, ‘I would not be surprised’
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz’s steady return to fitness has belied his rapid return to form, which has been almost instant since he played his first competitive match back at the US Open in September. Since then, the Spaniard has already won two ATP titles and is currently into the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters . Given how ravaged the field in the French capital is, it feels like there is nobody left capable of stopping him from adding a new piece of silverware to his already sprawling cabinet. And yet, as he silently moves through the draw and closer to his first Paris Masters title, it is Jannik Sinner and Ben Shelton who have been dominating headlines. After all, their respective coaching changes both came as great surprises, and have sparked mass speculation about how Carlos Alcaraz might react. Brad Gilbert backs Carlos Alcaraz to make coaching change Speaking on the latest Big T podcast , it was Brad Gilbert who shared his theory for what the future might hold for Alcaraz. After all, since Juan Carlos Ferrero departed his team around this time last year, he has made no major additions to replace him, instead trusting in the guidance of Samu Lopez to spearhead his development. Discussing Ben Shelton ’s decision to add Alcaraz’s old coach to his team, Gilbert actually made a bold prediction about the seven-time Grand Slam champion, noting: “I’m sure he’s eager to get to work and make some changes so he can close the gap on Sinner, Alcaraz, and Zverev, and his combined record against the three is not that great. “But honestly, I do believe now after what Sinner did, you know… I expect at least two, three, more guys in the top ten to make big changes, and I expect two, three, women, probably, that are playing the year-end championships, to make changes. “I think, actually, Alcaraz will make a move soon, and the guy to keep most eyes on, I think, is David Ferrer. “Because he’s all of a sudden stopping as the Davis Cup captain. Everyone thinks now that that’s a perfect solution to go to Jodar, but, you know, I would not be surprised if Alcaraz makes a move this off-season.” Elsewhere, Alcaraz recently discussed shock losses to Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev at the Paris Masters , as he seeks his first-ever title here. Chris Eubanks reacts to Ben Shelton hiring Juan Carlos Ferrero Shelton’s decision to hire Ferrero came completely out of left field, catching everyone by surprise. Chris Eubanks was no different, and chatting in that same podcast, he offered his honest view on the decision. “It completely caught me off guard as well,” the American admitted. He continued: “I’m sitting here kind of in this bit of a limbo period of wondering, who’s he gonna go with? Jodar seemed like the most logical choice, young Spaniard; he’s had success obviously with another young Spaniard. That’s kind of where I kind of think all my energy went towards. “And yesterday, you start to see the reports, and I go, this is actually a perfect match. Photo by Leonardo MUNOZ

item.title: Alex Whittingham learning about MSU rivalry, shares own rivalry experiences
item.description: There was a sizable turnover between the roster and coaching staff from a year ago to now, many of which have no experience in the battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy. One of those coaches is linebackers coach Alex Whittingham. On Wednesday with the media, he shared how all the new faces are learning about the intensity and physicality of the Michigan-Michigan State rivalry. “Mr. Jansen came in and he was great, gave us the whole background,” Whittingham said on Wednesday of Jon Jansen, former Michigan offensive lineman who spoke with the team this week. “I’ve been a college football fan for a while. That’s why I’m kind of familiar with it. I’m lucky to have been, you know, in the rivalries back in Utah, those games that they played the last eight years. I’ve seen NFL rivalries, which is a little different flavor to that. … So experience with rivalries and kind of how they work. Getting educated this week has been eye opening and good, and I’m very excited for this game.” An added bonus for Whittingham specifically is his room of linebackers has some unique experience with the rivalry. Graduate student Aisea Moa spent three years at BYU and then last season in East Lansing with Michigan State. Moa shared with the linebacker room what it was like to be on the other side of the rivalry. “We got Aisea Moa in the room, who is a Michigan State transfer, so he gives us an interesting perspective,” Whittingham said. “I had him speak to the guys in our linebacker room on Monday, just kind of give us a take on where they’re at on the other side and what they’re talking about. So that was good.” Just like any player, Whittingham has his fair share of experiences with rivalries. Another in-state rivalry was when he was a student at Utah from 2013-17, playing against BYU in the Holy War every season. Whittingham has very fond memories of that rivalry. “As a player, being able to go undefeated against the team down south in Provo, the other team, that was a good experience,” Whittingham said. “I enjoy that and look back on that often.” Then as a coach in the NFL, the rivalry between the Chiefs and Raiders was one that always had a little extra spark to it. And his introduction to the rivalry as a member of the defensive staff was tumultuous to say the least. “Back in 2018, we played in the Coliseum in Oakland,” Whittingham said. “Conveniently all the coaches got to the locker room, we set our stuff down, went out for warm ups and all that, and we came back and conveniently, the plumbing had overflowed out of the toilets and gone onto all our stuff. It was crazy how it happened. First and last time playing there for me, so that was inevitable, I guess.” Like many others, Whittingham has plenty of experience with rivalries. Despite not having played or coached in this particular game before, the team is doing whatever it can to prepare for what it will be like. item.title: Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. An EU patchwork, not a single rate European Union countries do not share a unified tax system for the sector. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. Greece’s 10% sits toward the softer end of that band, below France’s often-cited 30% treatment and above Cyprus’s 8%. The same patchwork is shifting elsewhere in the bloc. item.title: The economic benefits of the covid vaccines may be double what we thought
item.description: The covid-19 vaccines were costly to produce, but paid for themselves many times over Paul Christian Gordon / Alamy The covid-19 vaccines may have provided health and economic benefits worth up to $64.3 trillion in the first year alone – almost double an earlier estimate. Previously, researchers calculated that the $79.4 billion invested in developing covid-19 vaccines saw a return of between $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion globally in the first 12 months after their rollout. But now, a reanalysis of the data suggests it is actually between $6.43 trillion and $64.3 trillion. This means that for every $1 spent on the vaccines’ development, between $59.70 and $809 was gained in that year. “It is great to finally see this research published to demonstrate the enormous health and financial benefits gained from covid-19 vaccines, in comparison to the costs that went into their development and delivery,” says Hallie Benjamin at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. Read more Does each new covid-19 variant pose a significant threat? The $6.43 trillion figure is based on a cost-effectiveness analysis that is generally used in the health sector and factors in quality of life, while the $64.3 trillion figure is based on a cost-benefit analysis used in the public sector. Advertisement Both include data from 173 countries on averted hospitalisations, productivity losses and lives saved. For instance, one of the estimates Benjamin and her colleagues used came from modelling that suggested the vaccines prevented 14 million to 20 million deaths in their first year. The initial $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion figures were released when the research was in a preprint stage, before it had been peer-reviewed. “We made many changes throughout the peer-review process that strengthened the quality of our findings,” says Benjamin. The researchers originally used the Value of Statistical Life Years, which considers how many years a person would be likely to live because of the vaccine, a figure that would be lower if someone was older. As part of the peer-review process, they were advised to use the Value of Statistical Life. Team member Mark Jit at New York University says this treats life spans more equally and is aligned with recommendations for valuing mortality-risk reductions. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter The cost-benefit analysis figure also increased significantly due to a change from calculating the economic value of avoiding a death, says Jit. But the returns weren’t equally distributed. The researchers found that the vaccines had the highest returns in richer countries. This was probably because poorer countries accessed them later, so fewer lives were saved and fewer productivity and healthcare costs were averted, says Jit. The results are “a message about the need for being able to distribute the vaccines fairly to the people most in need around the world”, he says. Covid raises risk of heart issues in children

item.title: Tomb in Siberia reveals humans were using cannabis 2800 years ago
item.description: Researchers excavate a burial mound containing horse and human bones along with cannabis seeds Frozen Corpses Golden Treasures, T.Wallace & G. Casp A hair found in a 2800-year-old tomb in Siberia has yielded the earliest definitive evidence of cannabis being used as a psychoactive drug. But the history of such use is likely to go back much further. Genomic studies suggest that the domestication of cannabis plants ( Cannabis sativa ) was happening in China about 12,000 years ago , with people potentially exploiting it for oil and hemp fibre. Archaeological sites with artefacts made from hemp dating to 7500 years ago have been found in China and Japan . The earliest firm evidence of the plant’s use as a drug had been chemical traces on wooden braziers in China that implied humans were “smoking” cannabis 2500 years ago as part of funeral rites. Read more How a surge in ancient plagues 5000 years ago shaped humanity Now, Gino Caspari at the University of Bern in Switzerland and his colleagues have pushed the date back another 300 years with a find at the Tunnug 1 burial mound in the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia. Advertisement The royal burial mound dates to the time of the Scythians, nomads renowned for their military skills and horseback archery who spread across a huge swathe of Eurasia. In an excavation trench at the centre of the mound, Caspari and his colleagues recovered almost 1000 whole cannabis seeds. Radiocarbon dating indicated that they were deposited around the start of the 8th century BC, some 2800 years ago. Subscriber-only newsletter Sign up to Our Human Story Sign up to newsletter They also found a preserved human hair dating to the same time, and chemical analysis of it detected cannabinol, a compound produced when THC, the psychoactive compound found in cannabis, oxidises, alongside chemical signatures of THC itself, so the person is likely to have felt psychoactive effects . “It’s not often as an archaeologist that you get to drug test a person who has been dead for almost 3000 years,” says Caspari. He says we can’t say how the person consumed the drug – it might have been smoked or the seeds could have just been ingested. Given its presence in the burial mound, Caspari says the use of cannabis was probably related to a ritual funerary process. That could have been for a religious high, but he suggests there might have been a more sinister use. What were ancient humans thinking when they began to bury their dead? Claims that a small-brained hominin called Homo naledi buried its dead raise intriguing questions about ancient minds and why we engage in this peculiar practice The burial mound also contains the remains of dozens of sacrificed horses and some scattered human bones, which could be indications of human sacrifice. “If you’re trying to sacrifice a human, it might be easier if they’re not quite as resisting. item.title: Earth has captured a new mini moon — but it won't stick around for long
item.description: null Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas. The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29). The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027. Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun . QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it. According to the Minor Planet Center, the closest QQ8 will come to our planet during this stay is around 353,000 miles (568,000 kilometers). That is around 110,000 miles (177,000 km) further out than the average distance between Earth and the moon . Even if QQ8 were to come close enough to collide with Earth, it would likely be completely destroyed in our planet's atmosphere before it reaches the surface, as it is only around 6 feet (2 meters) in diameter. A fireball burns up in Earth's atmosphere. QQ8 would look like this if it entered Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: Xiong Yi via Getty Images) This is far from the first time Earth has snagged itself a mini-moon, more accurately called a temporary satellite. In fact, research last year suggested that our planet could be orbited by as many as six mini-moons at any given time, with many of these being fragments of our more permanent natural satellite, the moon. While QQ8 is tiny, it is larger than the average mini-moon. That is according to modelling earlier this year that suggested the average size for a temporary satellite is 75 centimeters (30 inches) across. The same modelling suggested the average stay for such an object would be around nine months. So if QQ8 was captured in April 2026, that means it should move away in January 2027. The researchers behind those findings suggested that, were Earth to gravitationally grip a space rock around 10 feet (3 meters) wide, it could serve as a mini-moon for 10 to 20 years.

item.title: NFL Insiders Discuss ‘Shocking’ San Francisco 49ers Trade Idea Involving All-Pro
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Leading up to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, the San Francisco 49ers are still being looked at as a team that could swing another deal. Of course, 49ers general manager John Lynch already added to the roster by trading a fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for DeForest Buckner. But there’s a sense that the 6-1 49ers might not be done. Interestingly enough, the latest 49ers trade rumor connects them to another All-Pro, but this time it’s at a position that’s already filled. Related: 1 Bold Prediction for Each Game in NFL Week 9, Including Bills-Vikings Could the San Francisco 49ers Trade for Jonathan Taylor? Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis in Week 6. Back in 2022, the 49ers paid a heavy price to trade for a First-Team All-Pro running back, trading a second, third, and fourth-round pick, plus a future fifth in exchange for Christian McCaffrey. Now four years later, could the 49ers’ front office be mulling a trade for another First-Team All-Pro RB? On Thursday’s edition of “ PFT Live ” Mike Florio and former NFL QB Chris Simms discussed the topic of Taylor’s trade market. According to Simms, some around the league have asked him whether the 49ers have any interest in trading for Taylor. Simms and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan are good friends, so those inside league circles often wonder whether the NBC analyst has the inside scoop. “I’ve had a lot of people, insiders people from organizations text me, saying, ‘hey is your boy, do you think he’ll trade for Jonathan Taylor?’ Which, I have no idea about. But that conversation, people within the NFL certainly think there’s a possibility there, which would be shocking to me.” Chris Simms on Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Like Taylor, McCaffrey is signed through the 2028 season, yet, CMC is also 30 years old. Yet, as Simms suggested, it would come as a “shock” if the 49ers once again ponied up and paid the price to trade for the top running back on the market. Yet, the 49ers clearly value having an excellent running game, and a 1-2 punch featuring McCaffrey and Taylor would definitely be the best in the NFL. Still, that doesn’t mean the 49ers will be the team that outbids others in pursuit of Taylor. Then again, it’s possible none of the teams meets the Colts asking price, which is believed to be similar to what the Carolina Panthers once got to trade McCaffrey. Related: 5 NFL Trades That Could Happen Before Week 9, Including Jonathan Taylor to… Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Valencia manager could field a five-man defence to stop Real Madrid in La Liga clash
item.description: Valencia manager could field a five-man defence to stop Real Madrid in La Liga clash Real Madrid are set to travel to Mestalla to face Valencia this weekend as they look to extend their winning streak to eight games. Jose Mourinho’s team are flying high on the confidence gained from their dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over AEK Athens . Los Blancos have proved to be an unstoppable attacking unit in recent weeks following some tactical tweaks from Jose Mourinho. Now, according to AS , Valencia manager Javier Aguirre is testing a five-man defence in training in an attempt to stop Real Madrid. Aguirre prepares a defensive reshuffle The Mexican manager has tested a back line consisting of Pablo Maffeo, Arnau Martinez, Pepelu, Cesar Tarrega and Jose Gaya. Arnau is said to be operating as the right-sided centre-back, while Maffeo and Gaya would occupy the wing-back positions. Valencia could field a five-man backline to stop Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre had already experimented with pairing Maffeo and Arnau against Elche, but the former operated in a much more advanced role. Against Real Madrid, though, Aguirre’s side will look to be as compact as possible defensively and prevent Los Blancos ‘ attackers from thriving. The proposed system is also said to feature Guido Rodriguez, Javi Guerra and youngster Aaron Mayol in midfield, with Arnaut Danjuma partnering Umar Sadiq in attack. The Nigerian recently scored Valencia’s winner against Elche and could return to the starting line-up against Madrid. A potential challenge for Real Madrid Valencia are always a difficult team to face at Mestalla , and they have become significantly more solid since Aguirre took over. This weekend would mark Real Madrid’s final league visit to the stadium, with Valencia set to move to a new stadium next season. Jose Mourinho’s men will face a stern test against Valencia at the Mestalla. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre’s approach appears designed to restrict Madrid’s attacking space, particularly in wide areas, while maintaining three central defenders to deal with Kylian Mbappe. For Mourinho’s men, breaking down such a deep block would require creativity and the likes of Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham to find a way through. With Vinicius Jr. still unavailable through suspension, Mourinho should have no problem playing the Turkish international against Valencia. A five-man defence would provide a new kind of challenge for Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, and it remains to be seen how they fare this weekend.

item.title: Report: Colts have received ‘plenty of calls’ on Taylor and others, but holding off until early next week
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Running back Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs for a first down in the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, the Indianapolis Colts have received “plenty of trade calls” on their readily available players, most notably of interest Jonathan Taylor, but are planning on holding off on executing any potential deal until after their upcoming Week 9 home game against the Dallas Cowboys: Sources: The #Colts have received plenty of calls on several players, including Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Grover Stewart and others. But the belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the… https://t.co/R9AJq2MRRR pic.twitter.com/1p08ZP9gIi — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 5, 2026 There’s been some reported thought and speculation around the industry that the Colts potentially moved too quickly on trading two of their veteran pillars, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner earlier last week, and did not possibly maximize the full trade return of either longtime organizational standout respectively. This may be a correction by the Colts, holding out hope of maximizing their available veteran players’ trade value, including Taylor and starting nose tackle Grover Stewart, as well as starting young slot wideout Josh Downs—who requested a trade from the organization last week. All of whom have appeared to garner trade interest, albeit to different levels of possible received compensation, from prospective suitors. The NFL’s trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th, at 4 PM EST. In particular, Taylor projects to garner a significant return in draft capital, but there’s increased speculation around league circles that the Colts are hoping for at least a “Christian McCaffrey” trade haul coming back to Indianapolis, if not, at least a first round pick entirely. To me, it makes sense for the Colts to hold out for better draft capital if they haven’t received the offer they’ve ideally wanted for each of their respective readily available players. The offers they have already received figure to largely still be there early next week, as they’re the major trade seller dictating this year’s trade deadline activity—with other teams reacting and following suit.

item.title: Lewis Hamilton backs claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than F1 rivals
item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton maintains Ferrari needs further talks to iron out its rules of engagement, backing claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams. Hamilton and Leclerc came to blows on lap one of last weekend's race in Mexico with both drivers going off the track at Turn 4, which eventually handed Max Verstappen a golden opportunity to snatch away the win and costing Ferrari a possible 1-2 victory, instead the duo finishing second and fourth. Hamilton was incensed by how hard Leclerc raced on the opening lap, only for the Monegasque to permanently stay ahead as he cut the track at Turn 4. Leclerc only received a five-second penalty for gaining a lasting advantage, with mitigation bringing that punishment down from 10 seconds. Their Mexico fight further fed suggestions that Leclerc appears to race his teammate harder than anyone else, having come after a Singapore Grand Prix in which Leclerc backed off at the start despite being fully on the inside of polesitter Max Verstappen. Leclerc did race the Dutchman hard at the subsequent US Grand Prix in Austin, however, overtaking the Red Bull man around the outside of COTA's Esses. When asked if the idea of Leclerc racing him harder than other drivers is something Hamilton has also noticed, the seven-time world champion replied: "Yes. I see what you see. In Singapore, he was fully on the inside into Turn 1, he had won the lead, and he backed off. It was definitely different. "But I mean, if you look at the team-mates, it was the same with Sebastian [Vettel]. It was the same with Carlos [Sainz]. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari As emotions ran high, Hamilton demanded talks to clarify the team's rules of engagement and warned of "big problems" for the squad. Motorsport.com understands team principal Fred Vasseur has spoken briefly to both drivers, albeit separately, after feeling the events of Mexico showed a lack of respect towards the team's 2000 people staff. But with Vasseur having travelled back to Europe in between races and Leclerc spending time with his family following the birth of his daughter, Hamilton says further talks are still needed. "Naturally I was frustrated, and I'm still frustrated," he said when asked by Motorsport.com if he views the events of Mexico in a different light now they have had time to cool off. "So, conversations need to be had. We will have those when the time permits. "We had an opportunity to win for the team. The team has done such an amazing job in bringing upgrades this year and I think they've done an incredible job. We've scored more points than any other team in the last three or four races. We could have easily had a one-two, so we definitely have to work towards making sure that doesn't happen again." item.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists. Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. “All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said. He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed. “Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said. Wike also criticised the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, saying Nigerians had already given him and other politicians opportunities to govern. “Nigerians know that Atiku and co have been given the opportunity, but they did not do anything. Nigerians know that the former governor of Rivers State looted our state,” he said. The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election. “I agree that Kwankwaso is very popular, but he ran in 2023 and won in Kano, fine, but what about the other northern states? What about the North-Central, what will happen there?” he asked. Wike further questioned whether Obi still enjoyed the level of financial and popular support associated with his 2023 presidential campaign. “The Obi wave is dead and buried. How many people are contributing money for Obi today?” he said. The post 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Joan Garcia opens up on adapting to Barcelona’s style: ‘I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper’
item.description: Joan Garcia opens up on adapting to Barcelona’s style: ‘I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper’ Being a goalkeeper for Barcelona is about more than just stopping shots. It is one of the most demanding roles in football. Playing in goal for Hansi Flick’s Barça is a whole other story. The goalkeeper must act as the last defender on a number of occasions and remain alert to the space behind the back line. Joan Garcia has embraced those responsibilities since arriving from Espanyol in 2025. He has emerged as the perfect goalkeeper for Flick’s Barcelona. More than a shot-stopper Speaking in an interview with GQ, the 25-year-old discussed his adaptation to Barcelona, his development as a goalkeeper and how he manages the pressure of representing the club. “I have always felt very comfortable helping the team in that aspect. It is true that at Barcelona it is much more necessary, and it is something I enjoy working on and practising to keep improving every day,” Garcia said. (h/t SPORT ). “I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper. I try to help in many aspects of the game and remain very alert to anticipate and prevent possible chances for the opposition,” he added. Joan Garcia kept his first clean sheet in the Champions League at Barcelona. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) These qualities are very valuable to Flick’s Barcelona. Joan has repeatedly timed his rushes off the line to perfection. He recently celebrated his first Champions League clean sheet for the Catalan club in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa. Garcia on handling pressure and mental preparation The Spanish international has also spoken about the psychological demands of goalkeeping, where one mistake can define a player. “It is something we goalkeepers live with from a very young age. We know the position carries enormous responsibility, but it is not something that affects me too much,” he explained. “Over the years, I have learned to manage these situations much better and, at certain moments, I have worked with psychologists. At this elite level, I believe taking care of the mental side is fundamental.” Joan Garcia is slowly entering the scheme of things in the Spain squad. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Despite being only 25, Garcia also recognises his responsibility towards Barcelona’s younger players. “I try to contribute my experience, help and advise my teammates in whatever way I can, even though I am only 25 years old,” he said. The former Espanyol shot-stopper has also entered the reckoning for Spain under Luis de la Fuente, although a starting berth seems far-fetched. Joan Garcia has performed exceedingly well in the season and a half since he joined the club in 2025. It remains to be seen how the 25-year-old develops and whether he can be the goalkeeper who brings the Champions League back to the Spotify Camp Nou.

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Chicago Cubs looking to make additions this offseason to boost their team, the one player who has been linked to the team in rumors is star pitcher Tarik Skubal . As rumors around the Cubs and Skubal continue , this MLB insider would speak on the potential of a partnership. item.title: BCCI announces major venue change for India-Sri Lanka series; 1st ODI moved from New Delhi
item.description: The opening ODI of India's upcoming home series against Sri Lanka has been shifted from Delhi to Visakhapatnam, with the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirming the venue change on Thursday. The December 13 fixture, originally scheduled to be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, will now take place at the ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam. Why has India vs Sri Lanka 1st ODI been shifted? The DDCA had approached the BCCI seeking a change in venue, citing its inability to host the international fixture amid renovation work and unfavourable weather conditions expected in Delhi during December. The association was concerned that the ongoing work at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, coupled with the possibility of weather-related disruptions, could affect the smooth organisation of the match. The BCCI subsequently approved the request and confirmed Visakhapatnam as the new venue for the series opener. India vs Sri Lanka: Revised ODI and T20I schedule Sri Lanka are scheduled to play three ODIs and three T20Is during their tour of India in December 2026. While the opening ODI has been moved to Visakhapatnam, the remaining five fixtures will continue at their previously allotted venues. The three-match ODI series will begin on December 13, followed by the T20I leg, which gets underway on December 22.
